$comment: Semantic overlay for the Jamcore OpenAPI document (https://d2jam.com/api/v1/openapi).
The published spec describes paths, verbs, parameters and auth requirements accurately,
but every request body is typed `{ "type": "object", "additionalProperties": true }`
and every response is the generic `SuccessResponse` envelope with an untyped `data`.
That is not enough to generate a usable client, so this file supplies the missing half.
Field shapes were derived from the public Jamcore backend:
- src/auth/gameToken.ts                    (device code / device token / game token shapes)
and cross-checked against live responses from https://d2jam.com/api/v1.
`operations` doubles as the scope filter: a path/verb in the spec with no entry here is
not generated. The generator prints everything it skipped so coverage stays visible.
As Jamcore adds real schemas to its OpenAPI document, entries here can be deleted.

fields.doc: Absolute URL to the avatar image.
One line profile tagline.
Profile biography, may contain HTML.
Twitch login name, if the user linked one.
ISO 8601 timestamp.
ISO 8601 timestamp.

The stored raw value. For SCORE and GOLF boards this is the submitted value multiplied by 10 ^ decimal_places; for SPEEDRUN and ENDURANCE boards it is a duration in milliseconds. Use D2JamLeaderboards.score_to_display() rather than reading this directly.
URL of the screenshot backing this score. May be empty.

Leaderboard.doc: A leaderboard attached to a game page. Created by the developer on the Down2Jam website; games submit to it by id.

fields.doc: One of SCORE, GOLF, SPEEDRUN or ENDURANCE. See the TYPE_* constants on D2JamLeaderboards.
Decimal precision for SCORE and GOLF boards. Ignored for time based boards.
How many rows the website shows per page.
When true only each user's best entry is ranked.
Every submitted score, unsorted. Use D2JamLeaderboards.rank() to order them.

Achievement.doc: An achievement defined on a game page. Created by the developer on the Down2Jam website; games unlock it by id.

fields.doc: Absolute URL to the achievement icon.
Everyone who has unlocked this achievement.

DownloadLink.doc: A platform download or play link on a game page.

GamePage.doc: One version of a game's page. A game has a JAM page and optionally a POST_JAM page.

fields.doc: JAM or POST_JAM.
ISO 8601 timestamp for the start of the jamming phase.

Game.doc: A game entry. GET /games/{gameSlug} is the only endpoint that returns leaderboards and achievements, so it is also the read path for both.

fields.doc: Only populated by the list endpoints, which flatten it from the jam page. GET /games/{gameSlug} leaves it empty; read jam_page.name there, or call D2JamService.page().

REGULAR, ODA or EXTERNAL.
The page as submitted to the jam. Only populated by GET /games/{gameSlug}, and the place its name, description and artwork actually live.
The post-jam page, when the team published one. Only populated by GET /games/{gameSlug}.

DeviceCode.doc: The result of starting a device authorization request. Show user_code to the player and open verification_uri in their browser, then poll poll_device_link() with device_code until it resolves. Prefer D2JamAuth.start_device_link(), which drives the whole thing.

fields.doc: Secret. Poll poll_device_link() with this until the player approves or denies the request.
Short code to show the player, e.g. ABCD-1234. Already embedded in verification_uri.
Absolute URL to open in the player's browser.
Seconds until the request expires unapproved.
Minimum seconds to wait between polls.

DeviceToken.doc: The result of one poll of a pending device authorization request. A denied or expired request comes back as a failed D2JamResult instead of a status here.

fields.doc: authorization_pending, slow_down, or approved.
The game's access token. Only present when status is approved; empty otherwise.
The player who approved the request. Only present when status is approved; /self does not accept a game token, so this is the only way to learn who just linked their account.
Human readable name for this device or install, shown to the player when they approve it on the website.
The game this token will be scoped to. The issued game token only ever works for this one game -- see D2JamService.game_slug.
Id of the leaderboard on the game page.

A number. For SCORE and GOLF boards, the value as a player would read it; the server multiplies it by 10 ^ decimal_places. For SPEEDRUN and ENDURANCE boards, a duration in whole milliseconds. Send an int unless the board declares decimal places, because the column it lands in is an integer. D2JamLeaderboards.submit() picks the right form for you.
URL of a screenshot backing the score. The website requires one on every submission, so treat it as effectively mandatory.
Accepted as an alias for evidence by the server. Prefer evidence.
Id of the achievement on the game page.

post /device/code.name: start_device_link
post /device/code.doc: Begin a device authorization request. Prefer D2JamAuth.start_device_link(), which drives the whole flow: showing the user_code, opening verification_uri, and polling poll_device_link() until the player approves or denies it on the website.

post /device/token.name: poll_device_link
post /device/token.doc: Poll a pending device authorization request. Returns authorization_pending or slow_down while waiting, or the game's access token once approved. A denied or expired request comes back as a failed result rather than a status field.

delete /self/game-tokens/current.name: revoke_current_game_token
delete /self/game-tokens/current.doc: Revoke the game token used to authenticate this request. Prefer D2JamAuth.disconnect(), which also clears the stored session locally.

get /self.name: get_self
get /self.doc: Return the profile of the logged in user.

get /self/current-game.name: get_own_current_games
get /self/current-game.doc: Return the logged in user's own game entries for the active jam. Useful for resolving your own game slug at runtime instead of hardcoding it.

get /games.name: list_games
get /games.doc: List published games. Leaderboards and achievements are not included here; fetch a single game for those.

get /games/{gameSlug}.name: get_game
get /games/{gameSlug}.doc: Return one game with its leaderboards (including every score) and achievements (including who unlocked them). This is the read path for both features.

post /score.name: create_score
post /score.doc:
Submit a score to a leaderboard as the logged in user.

The server responds with a message only, no score object. Prefer D2JamLeaderboards.submit(), which converts the value for the board type and can attach a screenshot as evidence.

delete /score.name: delete_score
delete /score.doc: Delete a score. Allowed for the score's owner, the game's team members and moderators.

post /achievement.name: unlock_achievement
post /achievement.doc: Unlock an achievement for the logged in user. Unlocking one that is already unlocked is harmless.

delete /achievement.name: lock_achievement
delete /achievement.doc: Revoke an achievement from the logged in user.

post /image.name: upload_image
post /image.doc:
Upload a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image and return its path on the API.

The returned value is relative (for example /api/v1/image/<uuid>.png); D2JamAPI resolves it to an absolute URL for you. Requires login, and the image must be at most 8 MiB.
